A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and the supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. However, v1 ends at the references and omits appendices it repeatedly cites; v2 includes Appendices A–D. This limits direct comparison of the earlier supplementary details.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations in Figure 2 and evaluations of ten target models on GPQA Diamond, AIME 2025, and GSM8K in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and reports additional robustness checks, repeated-decoding comparisons, and supplementary simulation and benchmark results.

M1.justification: The EIF, cross-fitted one-step estimator, and Monte Carlo correction in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. V1 already describes using a fixed LLM semantic regressor without cross-fitting; v2's Algorithm 2 and prompting details document that variant rather than establish a new estimation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian simulation setting and GPQA Diamond, AIME 2025, and GSM8K tasks. The added auxiliary-model, prompt, subset, and decoding experiments change procedures within this coverage, not the represented domains or tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds a repeated-Y baseline using 12 target responses for five GPQA Diamond target models in Table 6. The naive estimator and simulation Oracle comparator remain. Alternative auxiliary models are configurations of the proposed approach, not additional competing estimators.

E3.justification: New Section 5.3 substantially expands evaluation design: an alternative GPT-5 mini/QwQ-32B auxiliary configuration, another AIME subset, an N=25 subset, and a correctness-only judging rubric. It also compares one response plus 11 comparisons against 12 target responses. Original Tables 1–3 retain their settings; newly disclosed appendix details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Tables 4, 5, 7, and 8 add explicit checks of sensitivity to auxiliary-model choice, subset selection, subset size, and judging criteria. Appendices B and C additionally make noise-sensitivity and sample-size analyses inspectable; v1 mentioned these analyses but omitted their referenced appendices.

E5.justification: V2 reports an additional AIME subset selected with a different random seed in Table 5, without identifying the seed value. The simulation's 100 independent trials are unchanged. Neither version reports empirical confidence intervals, standard errors, or significance tests for the real-world comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 are numerically identical, and Figure 2 retains the same plot. V2 adds results for the robustness conditions and repeated-Y baseline; Tables 1 and 6 support its finding that one-step estimates are closer to the reference accuracy in four of five models under both configurations. Figures 3–5 and Tables 9–11 supply additional supplementary results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 supplies substantial mathematical material absent from the supplied v1: EIF projection, asymptotic-normality, variance-reduction, and orthogonality proofs in Appendix A, plus Gaussian derivations in Appendix B. These expand documented support rather than establish new theorem statements. Recasting Assumption 3.1 as Definition 3.1 preserves the same known-conditional-distribution model.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: comparative signals as control variates, an efficient asymptotically normal estimator, semantic regression for small samples, and validation on three benchmarks. The conclusion retains the proposed extensions to other auxiliary signals and metrics; its new applicability qualification is assessed under C2.

C2.justification: Remark 5.1 newly acknowledges finite-sample degradation with weak auxiliary signals and distinguishes variance reduction from pointwise dominance. The conclusion clarifies that precise estimation cannot repair benchmark invalidity. Section 5.3 also interprets the new checks as evidence against dependence on a particular auxiliary pipeline, subset, or rubric.

D1.justification: V2 provides a code-repository link and extensive implementation information unavailable in v1: a 32,768-token target limit, auxiliary limits of 8,192 or 2,048 tokens, explicit semantic-regression pseudocode, generation/judging/regression prompts, and a data example. These are newly documented details, not evidence that the original settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds model-source references and a qualification about Bayesian methods' sensitivity to priors, while removing several citations, including Jin et al. 2025a/b and Xu et al. 2025. The central positioning around semiparametric efficiency remains. The Lu-to-Yan attribution update concerns the same survey and is bibliographic.

P1.justification: Most shared prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include targeted clarification of the model specification and simulation indexing, wording corrections, updated cross-references, and the insertion of Section 5.3. Much of the added appendix length supplies scientific and implementation content rather than rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column main text with a two-column conference layout and running headers, relocates Figure 1 to the opening page, and consolidates Tables 1–3 on one page. It also includes Tables 4–11, Figures 3–5, Algorithm 2, and boxed prompt templates. The original simulation graphic and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Relative to the supplied v1, v2 resolves a substantial documentation gap by supplying referenced proofs, implementation details, and prompts, while adding targeted robustness checks and a repeated-decoding comparison. Its new limitations improve interpretation. The gains are qualified by absent real-world uncertainty intervals, a centering inconsistency in Appendix A.2, and Table 9's unsupported 18/20 improvement summary—the displayed estimates support 17/20. These issues temper the evidence but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in checkability and supporting evaluation.
